> **Figure 7.** A fully open-source surfaceome viewer. a) The viewer homepage, showing a table of all proteins with reference database membership, triage LLM calls, and deep-dive LLM calls. b) For proteins with a deep-dive record, a detailed page is available including both LLM information and deterministic results. Opening a protein’s deep-dive record reveals the complete structured analysis, including the surface-localization verdict and confidence, each graded attribute, supporting verbatim literature excerpts, and deterministic features. Together, these elements allow readers to trace every conclusion to its source. The Compare view lets a user upload their own protein set and see it scored against the atlas — surface calls, tiers, and evidence for each member — for rapid triage of a candidate list, in the spirit of enrichment tools like Enrichr [(Chen et al., 2013; Xie et al., 2021)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?J1RBaR). The exact agent prompts, a browsable table of the SurfaceBench benchmark with per-model calls, and the full reproducibility materials are also available as dedicated views. Because every call is exposed with its evidence and prompts, users can not only inspect the reasoning but flag errors: each record carries a feedback mechanism, and users may choose to make their feedback public to alert others to errors or missing information. We also welcome broader suggestions or contributions to enhance the site at <surfaceome-viewer@deliverome.org>. ## Discussion This version of the viewer and dataset catalogs which proteins are accessible at the cell surface and in what context; extending it along several axes would broaden its use. The current version of the viewer intentionally says relatively little about whether a given protein has been targeted therapeutically or has appropriate binding sites. While we include SURFACE-Bind sites as a starting point, assessing targetability is a highly modality-specific strategic question beyond the scope of this target-centric viewer. Similarly, we leave the clinical competitive landscape to resources like Open Targets, which track it as it changes. More broadly, we built the catalog to be combined with other data rather than to be a complete source on its own: a public API serves each gene's record, the full catalog, and the evidence behind each call. Users can then join our results with other public resources or their own internal data, or build them into their own analyses. We intend to extend the database in the near future to include additional target-intrinsic computational predictions, literature data, and our own and others’ experimental data in two key areas: 1) surface protein internalization and 2) quantity of protein present specifically on the cell surface. A significant goal of our work at Deliverome Bio is measuring and predicting these parameters to identify new internalizing proteins for precision therapies. For internalization, we aim to incorporate sequence-intrinsic prediction models alongside LLM-collated literature and experimental data, though such data are far sparser than for surface protein expression. We are also generating our own experimental internalization data, which we intend to promptly share via this viewer and established public data repositories. To facilitate design of epitope-tagged surface proteins, we are developing deterministic algorithms to predict suitable sites [(Lenaerts et al., 2025)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?EgnD1N) as well as LLM-based analyses to identify successfully tagged sites from the literature. We will also continue incorporating new deterministic features as they are published into the viewer, such as the newly available DeepTMHMM2 [(Teufel et al., 2026)](https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?Q8LLu4). For expression, we will integrate published scRNA-seq and proteomics data and add our own measurements. Two screenshots of the live surfaceome viewer at
[surfaceome.deliverome.org](https://surfaceome.deliverome.org) —
(a) the catalog homepage with the 24 deep-dive filter facets on the
left rail; (b) the per-gene detail page exposing the full validated
`SurfaceomeRecord` (executive summary, nine LLM-graded sections,
deterministic-features card with canonical DeepTMHMM topology,
AlphaFold pLDDT + structure links, orthologs, paralogs ≥ 80 % ECD
identity, SURFACE-Bind MaSIF patches, Schweke 2024 homo-oligomer
state).

Reproduce it with `uv run --with playwright make_web_preview.py`, which
screenshots the live site and rebuilds the SVG. There is no data TSV —
the inputs are the two pages themselves, so a re-run reproduces the
figure as the viewer looks *today* rather than byte-for-byte as
published. That is deliberate: it is how the panels get caught going
stale. The canonical generator is
[`scripts/figures/web_preview.py`](https://github.com/Deliverome-Project/accessible-surfaceome/blob/main/scripts/figures/web_preview.py).
Playwright drives a real browser, so Chrome must be installed.
The viewer's code lives at
[`viewer/`](https://github.com/Deliverome-Project/accessible-surfaceome/tree/main/viewer)
in the project repo and ships as its own Cloudflare Pages project;
the live URL above is the public deployment.
